new_jobs.title: Head of Growth & Marketing
new_jobs.description:
About High Camp

High Camp was born from a love of craft cocktails and the great outdoors. What began as a Kickstarter campaign has grown into a brand known for premium, beautifully designed products that are built to last and made to share.

We design Fortified Barware for people who care about what they pour, wherever they pour it. We make it easy to craft and carry your favorite drinks everywhere from the backyard to the backcountry.

We're a lean team that has grown primarily through a strong direct-to-consumer business. Now we're building toward true omni-channel growth across DTC, wholesale/B2B, corporate gifting, and marketplaces. This hire is one of the most important seats in the company.

Head of Growth & Marketing

About the job

As Head of Growth & Marketing, you'll own High Camp's acquisition, retention, and revenue performance across our direct-to-consumer business, our largest revenue channel, while supporting marketing needs across the broader company. You'll lead our creative and performance marketing team, translate brand direction into marketing that performs across every channel, and oversee the partners and systems that power growth and e-commerce. This role is a deliberate middle ground between a pure growth operator and a CMO: strong growth fundamentals come first, with enough marketing range to serve the whole company.

This role reports to our CEO & you’ll lead an in-house team across creative, performance, and organic, and direct a roster of agency and contract partners covering media buying, email and SMS, video and design, web development, and emerging channels. You’ll own a seven-figure media budget, the partner relationships behind it, and the decisions about how this capability is resourced as we scale.

What you'll do

Own DTC growth and e-commerce performance.
Hold the DTC revenue target and contribution margin, not just top-line revenue. Whoever executes the work, the outcome sits with you.
Partner with Finance on forecasting and reporting.
Build the annual and peak-season paid media budget and an inventory-aware DTC forecast, set efficiency targets, and review performance against plan regularly.
Lead paid growth strategy.
Own risk analysis and go/no-go calls on paid and marketplace spend, using incrementality testing to know where the next marginal dollar earns the most.
Run creative as a performance lever.
Direct our in-house creative team and creative vendors, and build the creative testing program and creator/UGC pipeline that feed paid performance.
Grow organic reach.
Set direction for social, PR, affiliates and brand partnerships, and make sure they build demand that paid and retention can convert.
Own retention and lifecycle.
Set email and SMS strategy, calendar and LTV goals, and own the repeat purchase and LTV targets that come with them. You’ll work through a mix of in-house and partner resources, and you’ll shape how that mix evolves as the business scales.
Own go-to-market, launches and promotions.
Plan launches around when product actually lands and around wholesale and corporate timelines, own the promotional calendar, and translate brand direction from the founders into channel execution.
Make marketing show up for the whole company.
Make sure the content engine produces assets our wholesale and corporate custom teams can use, and that paid supports where DTC and B2B overlap, like corporate gifting in Q4. When channels compete for the same product, creative or spend, make the call that's right for the company.
Own the analytics and marketing tech stack.
Make sure tracking and reporting can be trusted, decide what to keep or retire, and direct the technical resources who run it.
Build the team.
Shape the growth and marketing functions as the business scales, deciding what to build in-house and what to contract or partner. We expect AI and automation to be a real part of that answer, so the function grows on leverage rather than headcount alone.

Key requirements

Owned the number.
You’ve owned a DTC P&L or contribution margin line at a brand doing $20M or more, and can describe the efficiency targets you were accountable for.
Came up as an operator.
You started as a media buyer or close to it, and you’ve since managed media buyers or agencies rather than only executing buys yourself.
Proven creative testing
. You’ve directed a creative team or vendors producing high-volume, fast-iteration content, and built a testing or creator/UGC program whose results changed where spend went.
Planned around real constraints
. You’ve forecast demand where supply was limited (long lead times, seasonal peaks, constrained launches) and adjusted spend to match.
Retention results.
You’ve grown repeat purchase or LTV through email and SMS, including work with outside partners.
Hands-on measurement.
You’ve run a tracking or analytics implementation and can walk us through it. You’re fluent in growth math (MER, CAC, contribution margin, incrementality) and can pressure-test any buyer’s or agency’s plan.
Built growth teams.
You’ve built and led growth teams, decided when to hire, contract or partner, and directed technical or e-commerce platform resources.
Tools.
Deep Shopify literacy, hands-on with Meta, Google and TikTok ads, and working knowledge of modern attribution tools.
Location:
Remote-friendly across the U.S., with hybrid co-working options available in Bozeman, MT; San Rafael, CA; or Golden, CO.
Travel:
Two team retreat/collaboration trips per year to a hub location, plus 2–3 additional business trips per year as needed.

Nice-to-haves

You’ve supported B2B, wholesale, retail or corporate gifting alongside DTC.
Experience on both sides of the agency table, or running an agency selection or transition.
Incrementality testing and media-mix modeling, or experience scaling newer channels like AppLovin and TikTok.
You’ve worked on premium consumer goods, lifestyle brands, or hard goods, where the product itself carries the brand.

Salary & benefits

Expected base salary range (San Francisco Bay Area): $170,000 - $210,000 USD. Offered compensation will vary based on geographic location, as well as relevant experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance.

Eligible for target bonus of 20% of base salary
Choice of three PPO medical plans, with employee coverage on our base plan 100% company-paid
Dental, vision, and HSA plan options
Flexible PTO
401(k) with up to 5% company match
Monthly cell phone stipend
Paid parental leave (16 weeks for birthing parents, 12 weeks for non-birthing parents)
Remote-friendly, with flexible schedules in a high-trust, high-autonomy culture
Office hubs and bi-annual company offsites for in-person collaboration and community

High Camp is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic. Applicants must be currently authorized to permanently work in the United States. At this time, we are not able to sponsor employment visas or provide relocation assistance.

new_jobs.description:
Social Media Manager & Content Creator, STRIING

STRIING
 · Los Angeles · Part-time, up to 20 hours/week · Hybrid

ABOUT STRIING

STRIING is a newly launched swim brand, being built from the ground up. It is an experience-first bikini bar and workshop where customers build their own set on the spot. You will find STRIING at LA-area markets, collab events, and in a brick and mortar pop-up in Manhattan Beach, CA. 
STRIING is part of the Suite Creative Studio portfolio, an LA fashion product development studio specializing in swimwear, intimates, and activewear.

THE ROLE

You will own STRIING's social media and content from day one. This is a hands-on role: you plan the calendar, shoot and edit the content, write the captions, engage the community, and report on what works. You report directly to the founder.
This is a rare chance to build a brand's social presence from the ground up. Once performance is proven, the role can expand to other Suite Creative Studio portfolio brands.

WHO YOU ARE

This role is perfect for someone who takes initiative, goes the extra mile, and wants to own the results. You are flexible and available to attend brand events as needed, which will include nights and weekends from time to time.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Strategy and planning

Build and run STRIING's monthly content calendar, aligned to drops, markets, pop-ups, collabs, and swim season
Define and grow STRIING's voice: fun, inclusive, confident, and community-driven
Set quarterly goals per platform and adjust strategy based on performance

Content creation

Shoot and edit short-form video, photo, and stories for Instagram, TikTok, and Pinterest
Capture the custom bikini bar experience: customers building sets, try-ons, reactions, and finished looks
Go live from markets and events, and produce recap content after each one
Create product, styling, fit, and behind-the-scenes content showing how STRIING sets are made
Design social graphics, carousels, and templates within brand guidelines

Community and engagement

Respond to comments and DMs daily in STRIING's voice; route orders, customer requests, and event inquiries to the right person
Collect, organize, and repost UGC with permission
Promote upcoming markets and pop-ups so customers know where to find the bikini bar
Research competitors
Stay on top of trending content and algorithm updates for growth and engagment

Partnerships and events

Source and manage creators, ambassadors, and collaborators: outreach, gifting, deliverables, and tracking
Coordinate content with event hosts and partner brands
Help plan collab events and in-person activations

AI-assisted workflow

Use AI tools daily to work faster across ideation, scripting, caption drafts, editing, resizing, and repurposing content across platforms
Use AI for trend research, competitor scans, and turning performance data into clear monthly insights
Build and maintain reusable prompts, templates, and a STRIING brand voice guide
Review and refine all AI output so every post is accurate, on-brand, and reads as human

Analytics and operations

Report monthly on reach, engagement, follower growth, and traffic or sales attributed to social and events
Maintain an organized asset library with clear naming and usage rights
Support email and website updates with content and copy

Confidentiality

Keep unreleased styles, drops, and collabs confidential until launch; no proprietary Striing or Suite Creative Studio client material is ever posted or uploaded to AI tools

WHAT YOU BRING

2 to 4 years managing social media for a swimwear, fashion, beauty, or lifestyle brand
A portfolio of content you shot, edited, and wrote yourself, plus accounts you have grown
Strong phone-first shooting skills and editing in CapCut, Adobe (Lightroom, Premiere), and Canva, or similar.
Hands-on experience using AI tools in a content workflow, such as ChatGPT or Claude for ideation and copy, Adobe Firefly or Photoshop generative tools for images, and CapCut or Opus Clip AI features for video
Good judgment on when AI helps and when content needs a human touch
Deep fluency in Instagram, TikTok, and Pinterest formats, trends, and analytics
Comfortable on camera and going live
Highly organized; comfortable owning a calendar with little oversight
Flexible to attend brand events, markets, and pop-ups on nights and weekends from time to time
Must have reliable transportation

NICE TO HAVE

Experience growing a new or early-stage brand
Experience with influencer programs, paid social, or creator whitelisting
Experience with Kit, Shopify, or a scheduling tool such as Later or Planoly, ManyChat

COMPENSATION

$35 per hour.
Part-time, up to 20 hours per week to start.
Generous STRIING product allowance. 

HOW TO APPLY

Send your resume, portfolio, and links to at least 2 accounts you have managed to hotline@mystriing.com

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Beyond channel management, you will serve as both an analytical steward and a persuasive creative force, crafting compelling, high-converting ad copy and integrating paid media channels directly into our reporting tools for transparent, real-time ROI tracking. You will work closely with Product Marketing, Growth Marketing, Creative, Web, and Marketing Ops teams to build aligned, performance-driven campaigns that resonate with our specialized audiences. If you thrive on finding high-intent opportunities, relentlessly pursuing performance efficiency, and turning analytics into growth, you will play a transformative role in driving Axon's global mission.

None
Build and own the annual paid media plan, including channel mix, audience strategy, and testing roadmap, and present results, insights, and recommendations to stakeholders and leadership. 
Develop, launch, and optimize campaigns across paid search, paid social, programmatic and display, retargeting, YouTube, industry publications, and ABM platforms. 
Conduct ongoing keyword research and trend analysis to identify high-intent opportunities for campaign expansion and performance improvement.
Connect ad platforms with CRM, marketing automation, and analytics tools to ensure accurate, real-time tracking of ROI, attribution, and conversions, and report on performance with clear strategy recommendations and A/B testing opportunities for key stakeholders.
Monitor spend, pacing, and performance metrics, making data-driven adjustments and bid updates to maximize efficiency.

new_jobs.title: Marketing & Social Media Intern (Unpaid)
new_jobs.description:
UNPAID ACADEMIC INTERNSHIP — ACADEMIC CREDIT REQUIRED
Remote within the United States only | Marketing, Social Media & Short-Form Video

Compensation: This internship is unpaid. No wages, salary, or stipend are offered. Academic credit must be arranged and approved by your school; MoonArq cannot award credit. Please apply only if you understand and are interested in this unpaid, school-approved educational opportunity.

About MoonArq
MoonArq is a growing consumer brand offering a supervised academic internship for undergraduate students interested in digital marketing, brand storytelling, short-form video, and social media analytics.

What You Will Learn
Work with a designated MoonArq mentor to practice creative planning, video editing, and evaluating social content. Through weekly guidance, feedback, and a term-long portfolio project, you will learn to connect brand positioning with content decisions and explain what engagement metrics can and cannot show.

Supervised Learning Activities
• Research relevant social media trends and compare creative approaches across Instagram, TikTok, and similar platforms.
• Develop sample content calendars, captions, concepts, scripts, and storyboards for mentor review.
• Edit short-form video drafts using CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, or similar tools.
• Observe and practice the content approval, scheduling, and publishing workflow under supervision.
• Review non-sensitive social media metrics and prepare a brief learning report.
• Maintain a learning journal and complete a final portfolio, report, or presentation for academic evaluation.

MoonArq's supervisor retains responsibility for final editing, approvals, scheduling, and publication. Interns will not independently manage live accounts, maintain the business's ongoing posting schedule, meet business-critical deadlines, or replace regular staff.

Required Qualifications
• Applicants must currently reside in the United States and participate from within the United States throughout the internship. This is a location requirement, not a citizenship requirement.
• Currently enrolled in an accredited undergraduate program and able to remain enrolled during the internship.
• Able to obtain written school approval and enroll in a faculty-supervised, credit-bearing internship, field study, practicum, co-op, independent study, or equivalent course before the start date.
• Interest in marketing, communications, media, film, design, business, or a related field.
• Some experience through coursework, class projects, a student organization, or personal creative projects involving video or social media. Professional experience is not required.
• Clear communication, organization, and openness to feedback.
• Understanding that this is an unpaid academic internship.

Preferred
• Conversational Mandarin Chinese and/or Chinese reading and writing skills, particularly for collaborating on Chinese-language content. Chinese language skills are a plus, not a requirement.
• Familiarity with short-form video editing, captions, visual storytelling, or basic social media analytics.

Academic Approval and Schedule
Selected candidates may receive a conditional placement letter and learning plan for school review. Before any training, assignments, account access, or internship work begins, MoonArq must receive written department or faculty approval, proof of course enrollment, and any required work authorization, including CPT where applicable.

Dates, duration, weekly learning hours, and learning objectives will be agreed with the student and school before starting. The program will accommodate academic commitments and be limited to the period needed for the agreed learning objectives. It does not include a promise of future paid employment.

Application
Submit your resume and, if available, a link to existing class, student organization, or personal video/social media projects. Tell us your school/program, possible internship course or credit arrangement, availability, and any Chinese language skills. Do not create new unpaid work or disclose confidential material for your application.
